es: Exponer una teoría con pistas y dos grados de certeza distintos usando modales de deducción.

teaching.en: My theory is that someone must have been using the old library at night.
teaching.es: Mi teoría es que alguien debió de estar usando la biblioteca vieja por la noche.
teaching.explanationEs: My theory is that + frase: presenta lo que piensas; must have been marca certeza alta.
segments: My theory is that someone must have
been using the old library at night.
teaching.audioText: My theory is that someone must have been using the old library at night.

teaching.en: One clue is that there are footprints on the floor, so someone must have been inside.
teaching.es: Una pista es que hay huellas en el suelo, así que alguien debió de estar dentro.
teaching.explanationEs: La pista es un hecho que se ve; so lleva de la pista a la conclusión.
segments: One clue is that there are footprints on
the floor, so someone must have been inside.
teaching.audioText: One clue is that there are footprints on the floor, so someone must have been inside.

teaching.en: The evidence suggests that someone opened the window from the inside.
teaching.es: Las pruebas sugieren que alguien abrió la ventana desde dentro.
teaching.explanationEs: The evidence suggests that + frase: la prueba apunta a una idea, sin asegurarla del todo.
segments: The evidence suggests that someone opened
teaching.audioText: The evidence suggests that someone opened the window from the inside.

teaching.en: That would explain why the lights are on every night.
teaching.es: Eso explicaría por qué las luces están encendidas cada noche.
teaching.explanationEs: That would explain why + hecho: une una idea con lo que quieres explicar.
teaching.audioText: That would explain why the lights are on every night.

teaching.en: The mystery is not solved, but chances are that a student found a way in.
teaching.es: El misterio no está resuelto, pero lo más probable es que un estudiante encontrara la forma de entrar.
teaching.explanationEs: Chances are that + frase: un grado suave de certeza.
segments: The mystery is not solved, but chances are
that a student found a way in.
teaching.audioText: The mystery is not solved, but chances are that a student found a way in.

teaching.en: It can't have been the caretaker; he was at the match, and that is strong evidence.
teaching.es: No puede haber sido el conserje; estaba en el partido, y eso es una prueba sólida.
teaching.explanationEs: Can't have been + persona: descarta una posibilidad con una razón.
segments: It can't have been the caretaker; he was
at the match, and that is strong evidence.
teaching.audioText: It can't have been the caretaker; he was at the match, and that is strong evidence.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase da una pista (un hecho) y no una teoría?

choices.text: There is a red bag on the desk.
It may well have been a student.

feedback.es: «There is a red bag on the desk» es un hecho que se ve: una pista. Las otras dos son teorías con must o may well.

hint.es: Una pista es un hecho que se ve; la teoría es lo que tú deduces.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mi teoría es que alguien entró por la ventana.»

feedback.es: Se dice My theory is that…: la teoría «es» algo, no «dice» algo.

hint.es: Después de theory va el verbo be, no say.

origin.text: My theory ___ that someone came in through the window.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hay huellas, así que alguien debió de estar aquí.»

answer.text: There are footprints, so someone must have been here

feedback.es: La pista va primero y la conclusión después de so, con must have been.

hint.es: La pista va primero y la conclusión después de so.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la persona que habla.

choices.text: The speaker says what he or she saw.
The speaker gives a theory based on a clue.
The speaker asks a question about the rain.

feedback.es: La persona parte de una pista (huellas mojadas) y deduce con must have: da una teoría. No dice que lo viera ni pregunta.

origin.audio: There are wet footprints in the hall, so somebody must have come in from the rain.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada expresión con lo que hace en una teoría.

pairs.es: une la pista con el hecho

feedback.es: Cada expresión cumple una función: presentar la idea, dar una pista, conectarla con lo que se explica o descartar otra opción.

pairs.es: une la pista con el hecho

prompt.es: Completa: «No puede haber sido un estudiante porque el gimnasio estuvo cerrado.»

feedback.es: Because une la conclusión negativa con su razón: el gimnasio estaba cerrado.

origin.text: It can't have been a student, ___ the gym was locked all weekend.

prompt.es: Según las notas, ¿qué teoría es más sólida?

choices.text: The caretaker must have been working there.
The lights can't have been turned on by a person.
Someone must have come in through the window.

feedback.es: La taza de té y la ventana abierta apoyan que alguien entró. El conserje está de vacaciones, así que no pudo ser él, y la taza de té apunta a una persona.

origin.text: Notes from the librarian: the lights in the old library are on every night. Clues: there is a cup of tea on a desk, the window is open, and the caretaker is on holiday this month.

prompt.es: Completa: «La puerta abierta sugiere que alguien entró por ahí.»

feedback.es: Con sujeto singular, suggest lleva -s en presente: The open gate suggests…

origin.text: The open gate ___ that somebody came in this way.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo presenta la persona su idea.

choices.text: The speaker has an idea, but it is not certain.
The speaker has seen the student.
The speaker knows the student's name.

feedback.es: «Nobody knows for sure» y «chances are» indican una teoría con certeza suave. No se dice que vea ni conozca al estudiante.

origin.audio: Nobody knows for sure, but chances are that a student has been using the library at night.

prompt.es: Escribe tu teoría sobre las flores con tres pistas y dos grados de certeza.

answer.text: My theory is that a dog must have been getting into the garden at night. There are small footprints near the wall, so it can't have been a person. There is mud near the flowers, and the gate was open, so chances are that the dog came in that way.
accepted: My theory is that a dog must have been getting into the garden at night. There are small footprints near the wall, so it can't have been a person. There is mud near the flowers, and the gate was open, so chances are that the dog came in that way.

I think a dog may well have been coming into the garden at night. The small footprints near the wall suggest that it was not a person, and the mud near the flowers means it must have been a dog. The open gate would explain how it got in.

My theory is that a dog must have come into the garden at night. One clue is the small footprints by the wall, and another is the mud near the flowers. The gate was open, so it might have come in that way.

feedback.es: Una buena teoría nombra la idea, usa las tres pistas con so o because y mezcla un grado fuerte (must have, can't have) con uno suave (may well, might, chances are).

origin.text: Cada mañana faltan flores (flowers) en el jardín del colegio. Pistas: huellas pequeñas (small footprints) cerca de la pared (wall), la puerta (gate) abierta y barro (mud) cerca de las flores. Escribe tu teoría con las tres pistas, entre 40 y 70 palabras.

prompt.es: Escribe la teoría sobre la puerta de atrás y la cerradura.

answer.text: Someone must have come in by the back door, because the lock is broken.
accepted: Someone must have come in by the back door, because the lock is broken.
Somebody must have entered through the back door, because the lock is broken.
Someone may well have come in through the back door, because the lock was broken.

feedback.es: La teoría combina un grado de certeza (must have + participio) con la pista tras because.

origin.text: Teoría: alguien (someone) entró por la puerta de atrás (back door). Pista: la cerradura (lock) está rota (broken).

prompt.es: Según Sara, ¿qué piensa de la posibilidad de que alguien entrara?

choices.text: She thinks someone may have come in.
She is sure nobody came in.
She saw a person come in.

feedback.es: Sara dice «nobody could have come in»: está segura de que nadie entró, y atribuye el ruido al viento.

origin.text: Sara says: «The door was locked, so nobody could have come in. The noise was probably the wind.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «Eso explicaría por qué las luces estaban encendidas.»

answer.text: That would explain why the lights were on

feedback.es: That would explain why + hecho: conecta una idea con lo que se quiere explicar.
